previous_assumption: The append-only rule meant decision files could never be rewritten after creation, blocking lifecycle operations
correction: Append-only binds the CONTENT fields (assumption, correction, component, timestamp). Lifecycle metadata — status, retired_reason, superseded_by, last_confirmed — is amendable in place via updateDecisionLifecycle; that is the designed exception, not a rule violation

previous_assumption: One file per component (decisions/<component>.json, read-modify-write via temp+rename) was an accepted trade-off for a repo used by one dev — a concurrent write on the same component would just be rare
correction: matha is used by full teams with multiple agents, so same-component concurrent writes are a real case, not an edge case. Read-modify-write silently drops one of two concurrent decisions (last rename wins). Switched decisions/<component>.json to decisions/<component>.jsonl (one entry per line, pure O_APPEND, no read-modify-write) so concurrent writers can never lose a write. migrateLegacyDecisions handles the upgrade from both the pre-1.1 (bare-file) and 1.1 (grouped-array .json) layouts.
